answer: Enrollment uses a zero-knowledge nullifier: one legal identity maps to a rotating issuer, and only a per-human, per-epoch nullifier reaches the chain, so duplicates collide and are refused. Each locks a 200 POA bond for forty epochs, forfeited when a document is voided. Issuers audit each other, so a forged batch revokes every nullifier from it. Forged papers cost 120 dollars, so a thousand clones pay 120,000, and one collision erases them. Marble follows a delta's low line where the channel is cut; a duplicate shows one hand reaching twice, and walnut-hard bonds make that reach dear.
